newsitem.title: GERMANY: German film audiences at record in first half '97.
newsitem.headline: German film audiences at record in first half '97.

text.p: German film audiences reached an all-time record level in the first half of 1997, the Association for Film Promotion (FFA) said on Tuesday.

About 67 million people saw a movie in a theatre in the first six months of the year, marking a 10.2 percent jump from the same period the previous year. The FFA said the increase was largely due to a boom in new theatres.
"The bulk of the growth is linked mainly to new theatres and screens in addition to more renovated cinemas, which leads to more intense competition in regional markets," the FFA said.
It reported that cinemas added a net 27 more screens over the first six months of the year.

Multiplex cinemas -- new buildings with a minimum of seven theatres in addition to restaurants, public transportation connections and parking lots -- added 68 screens to the German movie landscape in the first half of the year, the FFA said.
The association said small cinemas have borne the brunt of this multiplex building boom, with 81 screens closing and many theatre-owners blaming mounting competition from multiplexes.
Turnover from tickets increased as well during the same period, with 683 million marks passing through Germany's 1,971 box offices, representing a 14.8 percent boost.

German films took a healthy share of that business, with the three top home-grown movies -- action film "Knockin' on Heaven's Door" and comedies "Rossini" and "Das kleine Arschloch" -- each drawing more than three million viewers.
The FFA said no American films had managed to draw that many Germans in the period in question.
